title: Orsen and the Garden
premise: Ada Yarrow, a royal food-taster who survives poison by building immunity one careful dish at a time, secretly keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild—a quiet trade in impossible things: bottled memories, borrowed luck, names that open doors. When a dying stranger presses a map of the Thirteenth Garden into her hands, Ada learns she is the last living signatory of a covenant between the human realm and the garden-folk, a pact broken by her own forgotten childhood. Hunted by the Guild's collectors and the crown's spymaster alike, Ada must gather her found family—a disgraced gardener, a memory-thief, and the prince whose food she tastes—to reforge the covenant before the moon completes its thirteenth turn. In the end, Ada chooses truth over loyalty to the Guild that raised her, sacrificing her own stored memories to seal the new pact, and wakes in the Garden with no past but every future.
about_author: Q. M. Marchetti is the pen name of a former botanist turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing seed banks across three continents. They write fantasy about people who keep dangerous records, and they still cannot keep a houseplant alive.

chapters.title: The Taster's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Ada. We meet Ada mid-service at the royal table, swallowing a suspect broth and surviving it, then slipping home to record the day's trades in the Vellum Guild's ledgers—memories, favors, small impossibilities. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness: Ada has made invisibility an art, and believes it will save her.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Ada. A dying stranger collapses into the Guild's back room, pressing a living map—one that grows like moss—into Ada's hands and calling her 'signatory' before expiring. The Guild's mistress orders the map surrendered; Ada lies for the first time. Emotional beat: fear curdling into defiant curiosity as the map blooms under her touch.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Owe
chapters.summary: POV Ada, with a brief interlude from the spymaster Corvane. Ada discovers her own name in the oldest ledger, dated twelve years ago, beside a covenant clause and a page torn out. Corvane begins asking questions at court. Emotional beat: vertigo—the life Ada built may be a wall built around something stolen from her.

chapters.title: The Gardener Who Fell
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Following the map leads to Wren Halloway, a disgraced royal gardener exiled for insisting the palace orchard grew fruit out of season. Wren recognizes the map and, reluctantly, joins Ada. Emotional beat: wary kinship between two people punished for remembering too well.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren explains the covenant: each full moon was a knot binding the realms, and the thirteenth turn—an intercalary moon—was when the two sides renewed their vows. The last renewal failed; the Garden is closing, and everything traded through the Guild will unravel with it. Emotional beat: dread with wonder, as Wren shows Ada a door that only opens on the thirteenth night.

chapters.title: Collectors
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The Guild sends its collectors—people Ada trained alongside—to reclaim the map, led by her old mentor Sable. A rooftop chase through the memory-market ends with Ada trading a year of her own remembered happiness to buy escape. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal; loyalty tested against truth for the first time in blood.

chapters.title: The Prince's Plate
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Cornered at court, Ada risks everything by telling Prince Ilan the truth: his favorite dish has been laced for years with a slow poison meant to make him pliable—and she has been quietly absorbing the dose. Ilan, furious and freed, becomes their ally inside the palace. Emotional beat: the cost of truth paid openly, and unexpectedly repaid.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable reveals why the covenant broke: the Guild's founders stole the thirteenth moon's name and locked it in the ledgers to monopolize the trade, and Ada's childhood memories were the price of hiding it. Sable offers Ada her memories back if she surrenders the map. Emotional beat: temptation rendered tender—the chance to be whole again at everyone else's expense.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Night
chapters.summary: POV Ada. On the intercalary moon, Ada, Wren, and Ilan breach the Garden as it seals itself, pursued by Sable and the collectors. At the covenant-stone, Ada reads the torn ledger page recovered from Sable and speaks her true name into the stone—but the pact demands a memory of equal weight to what was stolen. Emotional beat: climax, sacrifice chosen freely.

chapters.title: Orsen and the Garden
chapters.summary: POV Ada, epilogue-tinged. Ada gives up her stored memories—including her years with the Guild—to reforge the covenant, and the stranger's map is revealed as Orsen, the garden-spirit who pressed it into her hands to end his own long exile. Ada wakes in the Garden among her found family, pastless but unhidden. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; found family outlasting memory itself.
